newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Make HK a bridge between China and Britain--Cook.
newsitem.headline: Make HK a bridge between China and Britain--Cook.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it wants to see Hong Kong as a bridge in relations with China, after a 156-year colonial era ending in a midnight handover of power.
Foreign Secretary Robin Cook of the new Labour government met Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen in the last hours of Britain's rule.
He said he won an assurance that Beijing's new military garrison in Hong Kong would be involved only in external defence and not deployed against people in an internal security role.

The arrival of PLA troops, in the night hours surrounding the handover ceremony, has stirred anxiety over future potential military action against civilians, like Beijing's 1989 crushing of student-led democracy protesters.
Qian's response was in line with previous pledges that Hong Kong's internal security would be left to local police when Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China..
Cook underlined Britain's regret at the scale of China's troop deployment, involving a land, air and sea sweep by 4,000 troops, and said he did not see a need for armoured vehicles.

He told reporters: "We discussed mostly Hong Kong. We said we want to see China in the World Trade Organisation where we believe a large and growing trading nation should be. I also look forward to the future Europe-Asian Summit which Britain will be hosting.

"I expressed hope that Britain wants to see Hong Kong act as a bridge between Britain and China. But the success of that bridge will depend very much on the observance of the terms of the (1984 Sino-British) Joint Declaration that provides a firm foundation for the future of Hong Kong.

"I expressed our own disagreement with the decision to disband the elected Legislative Council. I asked for assurances that there would be an early election for a new democratic Legislative Council. Qian did give me assurance that it was the intention that there would be elections within the next 12 months."

"I expressed with regret that the Chinese PLA will be sent across in such large numbers although I recognise that China does have responsibility for external defence of Hong Kong. I asked the foreign minister for his assurance that they share our view that Joint Declaration provides for the Chinese army to play no part in the internal security of Hong Kong and I am pleased that Qian Qichen did confirm that China also agrees that internal security is a matter for the SAR government and not the matter of PLA"
